subject: HelioBank security review: data retention + request/response logging
messages:
From: Nate Hollis <nate.hollis@heliobank.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HelioBank Security Review <security-review@heliobank.com>
Date: Wed, May 14, 2025 at 9:17 AM
Subject: HelioBank security review: data retention + request/response logging

Hi Aisha,

Attaching our vendor security questionnaire. Two specific questions we need crisp answers on:

1) Do you log *customer prompts and model completions* in the hosted API?
2) Can we enable a mode with *zero retention / no logging* for prompts+completions (including in application logs, debug logs, and support tooling)?

This is a gating requirement for us.

Thanks,
Nate

[Attachment: HelioBank-Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-v4.xlsx]

---
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nate Hollis <nate.hollis@heliobank.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, May 14, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security review: data retention + request/response logging

Hi Nate,

Thanks — we’ll turn this quickly. Looping in our Security & Compliance team (Olga) and Solutions (Camila).

To confirm the ask: you’re looking for a *hosted API* configuration where we do not retain prompts or completions at rest (and ideally avoid emitting them into logs entirely), correct?

Best,
Aisha

---
From: Nate Hollis <nate.hollis@heliobank.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, May 14, 2025 at 11:28 AM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security review: data retention + request/response logging

Yes — hosted API. We can’t allow prompts or completions to be written to disk anywhere. If metrics need to be kept, that’s fine (counts/latency), but no content.

---
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nate Hollis <nate.hollis@heliobank.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, May 15, 2025 at 8:14 AM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security review: data retention + request/response logging

Hi Nate,

We do not use customer prompts/completions to train models.

For the hosted API: we currently retain request/response payloads for a limited period for debugging and abuse prevention. We can provide details on the retention window and how access is controlled.

A strict “no logging / zero retention” mode for hosted API payloads is not available today. If this requirement is firm, we should discuss Redwood Private (VPC) where the control plane and logging can be configured to keep payloads out of shared systems.

We’ve opened an internal support ticket to track your requirement and response (SUP-4821).

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nate Hollis <nate.hollis@heliobank.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, May 16, 2025 at 9:05 AM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security review: data retention + request/response logging

Nate — adding Alex (AE). Happy to walk through options. We’ve done “no customer content at rest” architectures in Redwood Private deployments; for hosted API we can share the current retention controls + access model.

Do you have flexibility to evaluate Private (VPC) if hosted cannot meet the zero-retention requirement?

— Camila

---
From: Nate Hollis <nate.hollis@heliobank.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, May 16, 2025 at 4:42 PM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security review: data retention + request/response logging

We can consider VPC/private, but we need clarity ASAP. Please send the hosted retention window + a statement we can include in our policy exception request.

Also attaching our logging addendum (what we mean by “no logging”).

[Attachment: HelioBank-Logging-and-Retention-Addendum.docx]
